evidence: The actual workbook Quality Checks!D26 and Internal Quality Checks!D26 require every dimension to use the live browser rather than source, memory or first paint; frozen quality-checks.md:108-110 applies that rule. Dimension paths below are beneath .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r1/task/tests/. gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1 and scored/visual/prompt.md:1 each say "Open http://localhost:3000 using Playwright" and explicitly prohibit source, bundles, filesystem, database-file and implementation inspection. scored/functional/prompt.md:3 imposes the same browser-only evidence discipline. Each judge.toml:6-12 resolves prompt.md and supplies playwright-mcp. test.sh:195-200 injects the actual app_context without removing those directives. This is more than a browser mention: render/prompt.md:5 plus render/judge.toml:23 require an invalid-password attempt followed by successful sign-in; constraints/prompt.md:5-9 plus constraints/judge.toml:23-25 require UI requisition/offer creation and fresh-context UI retrieval. functional/prompt.md:9-17 requires a live creation/readback gate, discovered UI request shapes and bounded replays; its P/B protocols require concrete mutations and readbacks, with restart followed by sign-in/readback at :49. polish/prompt.md:10-16 requires actual failed submissions, retained fields and successful retries, including real response-loss interception. visual/prompt.md:7-10 requires live creation/readback first, then all six operational screens plus harmless details/forms; it cannot be satisfied by one landing-page image. Scored prompts distinguish unobserved evaluator failures and deny unearned credit (functional:11, polish:16, visual:12). Relevant runtime evidence is limited but real: local/mcp.cjs:35-52 records JSON-RPC tool requests/responses, :80-107 performs live sign-in/UI creation and independent-context UI readback. local/mcp/requests.jsonl:3-5 and responses.jsonl:4-5 show browser_navigate and browser_run_code_unsafe calls, created=true, freshContext=true, separateUiLogin=true and the saved $50,000.01 record. This used pinned Playwright MCP 0.0.79/Linux Chromium on local port3032 and is tool-feasibility evidence, not a configured judge session or score. Verified current raw-evidence-index entries: mcp.cjs SHA256 91524d29b805eb616869c889fd1e5b7d5cabc5e8e84711c438a34730e0af90a6; requests.jsonl a47c870d86ccacdd9225d078e7ec32eee1a983dbc38c02faab9d1295c051c306; responses.jsonl ec85ba9e0d149d833f3623fd701eecf424067ffb75eadb8075c60f8e3004c1c3; results.json bad8d80ee96bda6a46775d4dfcc508371b96c50e3106cd9f4e27ffee1a6e4cc3. All 13 sourceBefore/sourceAfter app hashes match frozen task bytes; all 37 frozen task and 34 rules files match manifest hashes. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md matches its bound hash 9fa534809d9d5ddb99b141c7ee213bae35006ef49c7af4be0a6b14bbbbaf7b5b. This verdict establishes prompt direction, with supporting browser tool feasibility; it does not establish full configured judge completion, workload, reward discrimination, Oracle score or portal acceptance.
counterexample: Adversarial source review: a polished static login/workspace image or localStorage-only mock with prefilled offer figures cannot meet the invalid/valid sign-in, newly named UI creation and empty-context retrieval directives; source comments claiming correctness cannot substitute because every prompt forbids implementation evidence. Conforming-alternative review: a server-backed app with generated IDs, different routes/labels, native forms and initially empty operational collections remains inspectable because constraints/prompt.md:7-9, functional/prompt.md:13-17, visual/prompt.md:10 and app_context.md:21-27 require discovery by intent and accept equivalent product representations. These are reasoned counterexample checks, not extra executed app variants.
